title: Calcutta High Court: A Writ Petition Cannot Be Used to Stop Personal Insolvency Proceedings Under the IBC
case_name: Sanjay Jhunjhunwala & Ors. v. Piramal Finance Ltd. & Ors.
citation: W.P.A. No. 27091 of 2025, judgment dated 3 December 2025
card_summary: Personal guarantors facing a Section 95 IBC application filed a writ petition, arguing the borrower had largely repaid its dues. Justice Krishna Rao dismissed the petition as not maintainable: once a Section 95 application is filed, the NCLT, not a writ court, decides whether it should continue, since early interference would defeat the Code's design.
card_tip: Raise objections to a Section 95 IBC application, including part-repayment by the borrower, before the NCLT, not by writ petition; a writ court will not substitute for the Tribunal at this stage.
verification_notes: Chosen for the IBC & Insolvency category with a direct Kolkata angle since the Calcutta High Court decided it and personal guarantor insolvency is a growing dispute category for NBFC lending in West Bengal. Case name, writ petition number, 3 December 2025 date and the core holding (writ not maintainable, NCLT is the proper forum, reliance on the Farooq Ali Khan line of authority) are confirmed across two independent reports (Bar and Bench, Taxscan), with the order also available on Indian Kanoon. Not covered elsewhere on the site, which has general personal guarantor insolvency guides but not this specific ruling on writ maintainability.
